I was recommended this place to get some tests done on my dog, who was already having a lot of problems. From the moment they opened the door, the woman who answered was incredibly rude. She didn't even say good morning. Her first comment was whether I had made an appointment, to which I replied that I didn't know I needed to make an appointment. She responded, "Let's see if you can see her because they're very busy." She went inside to check, and as she was leaving, I got a call. The woman started asking me for information while she could see I was on the phone, so I asked her to give me a moment. After the call ended, I sat for a while waiting for the woman to come out again, which she didn't. So I went to the door to peek in and let her know I was finished, but I didn't see her. I did see, and they saw me, two people talking (women in uniform). I assumed they were in charge of taking the tests, but they didn't bother to ask if I needed anything or to let the woman know I was looking for her. A few minutes later, seeing that no one was coming out, I peeked in again, and they saw me again, doing nothing. So I went back inside and asked the woman to return the order for the tests that I had given her when I arrived. She gave it back to me with a surprised look when I told her I was leaving. I commented that they provided terrible service and that I didn't understand how, when they got referred clients, instead of providing good service, they seemed annoyed to help them. She just reacted with indifference.

I will never return to that place and I absolutely do not recommend it; they don't seem to care about the animals and they don't provide good customer service.

"Thank you so much for your review, Moisés! We're so glad to hear you had a great experience with our veterinary X-ray service and that you found the price reasonable. We're always here for you and your pet. Best regards from the Daltrhe Veterinary Clinic team!"

I took my dog ​​for an ultrasound to check his abdominal organs. The doctor who performed the study was very kind and quick, explaining what she saw. The ultrasound took maybe 10 minutes or less. Very satisfied with the service, 10/10.

Excellent service.
Thank you so much for your excellent rating, Joc Alv! We're so glad to hear you had a great experience with us. It's always a pleasure to serve you and your pet. We're here for anything you need!
Fast and professional service.
"Thank you so much for your recommendation, Laura! It's wonderful to know you trusted us with your kitten's care. We're here for you whenever you need us!"

"Hello, Angel! Thank you so much for visiting us and for sharing your rating. We're glad to hear you had a good experience at the clinic. We're here for you and welcome any feedback that will help us reach 5 stars next time. Best regards!"

I've taken my dog ​​to this vet several times and he's always received good care. However, on this last visit, I was very dissatisfied with how they handle the sale of medications.

When the treatment was finished, I had DOUBLE the amount of pills left over. I thought it was a mistake, but when I contacted them, they confirmed that this is their protocol: to sell a larger quantity so there's enough during the treatment and keep the extra "in case the pet relapses."

Personally, I found this practice to be an excessive and unnecessary charge. In over eight years of taking pets to different vets, they've never sold me full boxes of medication. They've always given me only the tablets needed to complete the treatment and charged me only for that amount.

I'm not going to self-medicate my dog ​​in the future with an antibiotic or any other medication just because I had some left over. If my dog ​​gets sick again, the right thing to do is have a veterinarian re-evaluate him and determine what treatment he needs. Therefore, the leftover medication will most likely end up going to waste.

I believe they should only dispense the amount of medication each patient actually needs. A veterinary clinic should prioritize the appropriate treatment for the pet, not sell entire boxes as if it were a pharmacy. That experience left me dissatisfied with the service.

If I could give them zero stars, I would. I took my dog ​​for an ultrasound with a suspected foreign object in his digestive tract, and the "diagnosis" was a presumed kidney tumor. This completely contradicted my vet's initial diagnosis, and if I hadn't had him admitted to the hospital and they hadn't repeated the test to confirm the presence of a foreign object and performed emergency surgery, my dog ​​would surely have died as a result of their misdiagnosis. It's unacceptable that they come up with this kind of nonsense just because they have "affordable prices."
Highly recommended! They did an ultrasound on my dog ​​and it was very quick, very affordable, and they treated her very well.

"Hello Leila! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating. We're so glad to hear you had a great experience with us at Daltrhe Veterinary Clinic. We're here for you if you need anything!"

I think they're good doctors. But they're very uncaring with our pets; they examine them as if they were objects, not living beings. Even the way they look at them is indifferent. I don't like that. Unfortunately, veterinarians are now more like businesspeople and merchants than doctors. To give you an idea, the cold, impersonal service is similar to what you'd find at ISSSTE and IMSS clinics. It should be called "DALTRHE Wellness Clinic." By the way, their business cards say they offer hospitalization, but apparently that's not the case.

She said all of this from the street; she didn't even open the door for me.

We'd always received excellent service, but today we left with a terrible impression. We requested information via WhatsApp about some tests for our cat, and they said it was no problem. We made an appointment and brought our cat in, paying for a taxi to wait for us. Our sick cat was fasting, and upon arrival, the receptionist was incredibly rude and arrogant. From the moment she greeted us, she made faces and rude comments. In the end, they told us they weren't going to do the tests because the prescription was from another vet who "probably" wouldn't accept them. That's not the problem, though. The problem is that they didn't clarify this via message and made us make the trip, keep our pet fasting, and on top of everything else, what bothered us most was the attitude, especially of the receptionist. It's a shame because our pets had been their patients several times before.

In response to what you wrote: I find it very concerning, as they aren't taking into account the patient's medical condition, which one describes upon arrival, and that's very serious. It's not a matter of overprotection; it's a matter of care and attention, and I find their behavior very troubling. This is how my dog ​​is now, bleeding due to malpractice.

Initial message: I don't usually post things like this, but I think that people who work with animals should hire people who feel the same love and respect for them. On my one and only visit to this clinic, I took my dog ​​for an X-ray, but the receptionist, an older woman who seems to lack compassion, didn't know how to handle my dog, even though they were informed from the beginning that she had a tumor and jaw problems. If they can't calm the pets for tests, why not ask the owner or person in charge of the pet to handle it? Why not ask the owner to take the dog out of the examination room? Be more responsible and more humane. That's the bare minimum we require when we take our pet for a checkup at a clinic. Thank you.

I came just to see the facade. The veterinarians are quite good and friendly. They explain everything.
And the prices are quite reasonable, which is much appreciated considering I have three pets.
The only downside is parking, but the service is good.

The woman who serves you is incredibly rude. She always makes faces when she helps you. When I first started going there for BARF food, I would call to check if they had it in stock, reserve the amount, and when I arrived to pick it up, she'd say, "Oh no, we're out."

When you call to verify if they're open and will be serving customers during the hours listed online, they say they close half an hour early, and when you arrive, they tell you, "No, we're not open anymore. I already turned everything off. Those are the old hours." They did that about three times.

On top of that, they misdiagnosed my dog ​​with a "chicken allergy," and he actually had a skin infection.

Terrible service in every way.

I took my kitten in because he needed a bladder ultrasound. My vet recommended it. The person who answered the phone was incredibly kind. When I arrived for an emergency appointment, everything was fine; I only had to wait a few minutes. However, when I got the results, I asked if they thought surgery was necessary (I just wanted a second opinion on what was wrong with my kitten). But the woman was a bit rude, telling me tactlessly that "they couldn't tell me if my cat needed surgery or not, that it depends on the vet's diagnosis." I understood, but she didn't have to be so harsh. I thought it was easy to ask because I thought she was a doctor, and in my desperation, I just wanted to know if it was serious. It was the first time I'd ever been through anything like this.

Other than that, everything was fine. They charged me $600.
